question.text: Scenario: Vikram Mehta, a CFA charterholder with 7 years of experience in wealth management at a private bank, wants to set up his own investment advisory firm. He plans to register as an individual Investment Adviser with SEBI under the SEBI (Investment Advisers) Regulations, 2013. His wife Neha is an AMFI-registered mutual fund distributor who currently serves 50 clients. Vikram expects to start with 100 clients, charging an annual fee of Rs. 25,000 per client. One of his prospective clients, Mr. Rao, has assets worth Rs. 2 crore and wants both advisory and distribution services from the same family. Under SEBI IA Regulations, an individual Investment Adviser can serve a maximum of 300 clients and must apply for in-principle registration as a non-individual IA if clients exceed 300 or advisory fees collected during the financial year exceed Rs. 3 crore. A part-time Investment Adviser is limited to 75 clients. Accepted professional qualifications include CFA Charter, among others listed in the workbook. The IA must additionally hold a valid NISM Investment Adviser certification. Records of investment advice, rationale, and client interactions must be maintained for a minimum of 5 years. An annual compliance audit by a CA is mandatory. Importantly, a family member of an individual IA shall not provide distribution services to the client advised by the IA, ensuring segregation of advisory and distribution activities. Question 4 of 5: Under what circumstances would Vikram be required to apply for in-principle registration to convert his individual IA registration to a non-individual IA registration?

answer.text: When his clients exceed 150 or his annual fees exceed Rs. 1 crore
When his clients exceed 500 or his annual fees exceed Rs. 5 crore
When his clients exceed 300 or his fees collected during the financial year exceed Rs. 3 crore
When his clients exceed 300 and his fees collected during the financial year simultaneously exceed Rs. 3 crore

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook says an individual IA whose number of clients exceeds 300, or whose fee collected during the financial year exceeds Rs. 3 crore, must apply for in-principle registration as a non-individual IA. Either threshold, on its own, triggers the conversion requirement. The Trap: Using "and" instead of "or" requires both thresholds to be crossed simultaneously — that is not what the workbook says. The 150/Rs. 1 crore and 500/Rs. 5 crore numbers are not the regulatory thresholds. Note: The conversion trigger uses the financial-year fee figure and the live client count — both should be monitored at year-end (and during the year) to know when to apply.
